payload.unusable_reason: Constitution Bench reference on a point of law only: whether an LMV licence holder may drive a transport vehicle under 7,500 kg without a separate endorsement. The reference was answered and the appeals sent for listing before a regular bench; no compensation amount is decided or stated.

journey.note: Inferred: the judgment does not name the tribunal or give its award or date for the lead case; it says only that the reference arises from compensation claims.
The Rajasthan High Court decided the lead civil miscellaneous appeal (registered in 2011) on 4 August 2017. Who appealed and any amount are not stated.
Insurer's appeal. A five-judge bench answered the licensing question referred to it and directed the appeals to be listed before a regular bench. No amount decided.

precedent.holding: A driver with a Light Motor Vehicle licence may drive a transport vehicle with gross vehicle weight under 7,500 kg without a separate transport-vehicle authorisation. The extra eligibility conditions for transport vehicles apply only to vehicles over 7,500 kg; special rules for e-carts, e-rickshaws and hazardous goods remain. Mukund Dewangan (2017) is upheld.

extraction.title_anon: Insurer's appeal on LMV licences for light transport vehicles, Rajasthan (Constitution Bench, no award)
extraction.family_summary: This judgment decides no compensation amount: five Supreme Court judges answered a question of law that had divided courts for years. Insurers often disputed claims when a light goods or passenger vehicle was driven by someone holding only a Light Motor Vehicle licence; in November 2024 the Court ruled this licence is enough for transport vehicles under 7,500 kg, so insurers cannot use that technical plea to defeat a legitimate claim. The lead case, an insurer's appeal from a 2017 Rajasthan High Court order in an appeal registered in 2011, was sent back to a regular bench after about 13 years. Insurers told the Court that compensation ordered by the lower courts was paid or would be paid.
what_mattered: The Act defines a Light Motor Vehicle as including a transport vehicle of not more than 7,500 kg, so the Court held the extra transport-vehicle licence rules apply only to medium and heavy vehicles.
Insurers produced no data showing that LMV licence holders driving light transport vehicles cause more accidents, so road-safety fears did not change the result.
Earlier rulings that let insurers refuse on this ground (Prabhu Lal, Roshanben Rahemansha Fakir, Angad Kol) were overruled; special rules for e-carts, e-rickshaws and hazardous goods still apply.
